course.title: Fitness Coaching Basics
course.tagline: Coach others to get fit: programs, form and the business of training.

days.title: What a fitness coach does
days.goal: Learn what a coach does each day and what makes a good one.

video.title: How to Build Muscle as a Beginner | Complete Gym Guide

steps: Watch the video and write down 3 jobs a coach does.
Write one sentence that says what a coach is in your own words.
List 3 ways a coach helps a client who is new to exercise.
Ask a friend what they would want from a coach and write it down.
days.task: Write a short note: what a coach does, in 5 lines.
days.challenge: Explain what a coach does to a friend in under 1 minute.

quiz.q: What is the main job of a fitness coach?
options: Help people exercise safely and reach their goals
quiz.explain: A coach guides safe exercise and helps clients reach goals they set together.

quiz.q: What should a coach do before giving a client hard exercise?
options: Learn about the client's health and past injuries
Ask them to lift as heavy as they can
quiz.explain: Knowing health and injuries first keeps the client safe.

quiz.q: What makes a client trust a coach?
options: Giving the same plan to everyone
quiz.explain: Listening and keeping promises builds trust.

days.title: Meet a new client the right way
days.goal: Learn how to run a calm, friendly first session.

video.title: How I'd Start Fitness Coaching From Zero: The First 90 Days

steps: Watch the video and note the first 3 things the coach does.
Write 5 simple questions to ask a new client.
Practise asking each question out loud in a calm voice.
Write a simple 30-minute plan for a first session.
days.task: Write your first-session plan on one page.
days.challenge: Explain your plan to a friend in under 2 minutes.

quiz.q: What should happen first in a first session?
options: A friendly talk about goals and health
quiz.explain: A talk first tells you what the client needs and builds trust.

quiz.q: Why ask about past injuries?
options: Because it is a rule with no reason
So you can avoid moves that could hurt them
quiz.explain: Knowing injuries helps you pick safe moves.

quiz.q: How long should a first session plan be?
quiz.explain: A short, simple first session keeps a new client comfortable.

days.title: Ask good questions and really listen
days.goal: Learn to ask questions that help you understand a client.

video.title: How To Become A Fitness Coach? Your Ultimate Guide With 10 Essential Steps

steps: Write 5 open questions. An open question needs more than a yes or no answer.
Practise one question with a friend and write down their full answer.
List 3 signs that show someone is really listening.
Write down one time you felt heard, and what the person did.
days.task: Have a 5-minute talk with a friend using only open questions.
days.challenge: Ask a friend about their health goal and repeat it back in your own words.

quiz.q: What is an open question?
options: A question with one right answer
A question you ask while walking
A question that needs more than yes or no
quiz.explain: Open questions get people talking so you learn more.

quiz.q: Why repeat a client's goal back to them?
options: To check you understood it right
quiz.explain: Repeating back checks your understanding and shows you listened.

quiz.q: What shows you are listening?
options: Eye contact, nods and short replies like I see
quiz.explain: Small signs like nods show you are paying attention.

days.title: Set goals clients can reach
days.goal: Learn to set clear goals that are small enough to reach.

video.title: How To Become A Fitness Coach? Your Ultimate Guide: 10 Essential Steps To Becoming A Top Fitness Coach!

steps: Write one big goal, then break it into 3 small steps.
Turn a vague goal like get fit into a clear goal with a number and a date.
Write one goal for a pretend client who has never exercised.
Check your goal: can you measure it? Can you reach it in 4 weeks?
days.task: Write 3 clear goals for a pretend beginner client.
days.challenge: Take a vague goal and make it clear in one sentence.

quiz.q: What makes a goal clear?
options: It has a number, a deadline and a simple action
quiz.explain: A number and a deadline let you know when you reached it.

quiz.q: Why break a big goal into small steps?
options: Small steps are a waste of time
Small steps feel doable and keep people going
quiz.explain: Small wins build confidence and keep clients going.

quiz.q: Which goal is best for a beginner?
options: Walk 20 minutes, 3 times a week, for 2 weeks
quiz.explain: A small, steady goal is safe and reachable.

days.title: Teach the squat, step by step
days.goal: Learn to teach a bodyweight squat in simple steps.

video.title: FREE NASM CPT Study Guide (2026): A 12-Week Plan to Pass

steps: Watch the video and write down each step of the squat.
Practise the squat yourself: feet wide, chest up, sit back like sitting in a chair.
Do 10 slow squats and check your knees point the same way as your toes.
Write 3 short cues. A cue is a short hint, like chest up.
days.task: Teach the squat to a friend using only your 3 cues.
days.challenge: Do 10 squats with a 3-second slow lower down.

quiz.q: Where should the knees point in a squat?
options: The same way as the toes
quiz.explain: Knees following the toes keeps the knee safe.

quiz.q: What should the chest do in a squat?
quiz.explain: A lifted chest keeps the back safe and balanced.

quiz.q: What is a coaching cue?
options: A short hint that helps someone move well
quiz.explain: A cue is a short, clear hint like chest up.

days.title: Teach the push-up, step by step
days.goal: Learn to teach a push-up and its easy versions.

video.title: Best Way To Run A First Session With A New Client || Trainer Tips and Solutions

steps: Watch the video and list the steps of a good push-up.
Practise a wall push-up: hands on a wall, body straight, bend and push.
Try a knee push-up on the floor and keep your body in one straight line.
Write 3 cues for the push-up, like body straight as a board.
days.task: Teach a wall push-up to a friend in 3 steps.
days.challenge: Do 5 slow push-ups from your knees with a straight body.

quiz.q: What should the body look like in a push-up?
options: One straight line from head to heels
quiz.explain: A straight line keeps the back safe and works the right muscles.

quiz.q: What is a good first push-up for a beginner?
options: A push-up with a heavy bag
quiz.explain: A wall push-up is easy to do with good form.

quiz.q: Where should the hands go?
options: Under the shoulders, a little wider than the shoulders
quiz.explain: Hands under the shoulders give a strong, safe push.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 1: Run a first session
days.goal: Put week 1 together: run a full first session with a practice client.

video.title: Squat Exercise Technique

steps: Pick a friend to be your practice client.
Write your plan: talk, health questions, goals, 3 easy moves.
Run the session for 30 minutes and use your cues.
Ask your client what felt good and what was unclear.
days.task: Run a full 30-minute first session and write down what happened.
days.challenge: Run the session without looking at your notes.

quiz.q: What comes first in a first session?
options: A talk about goals and health
quiz.explain: Talking first keeps the client safe and comfortable.

quiz.q: How many moves should a first session have?
quiz.explain: A few easy moves let the client learn without getting wiped out.

quiz.q: What should you ask at the end?
options: What felt good and what was unclear
quiz.explain: Asking for feedback helps you get better.

project.title: Run a first session
project.brief: Coach a practice client through a friendly 30-minute first session: talk, health questions, goals and 3 easy moves.
checks: Wrote notes on what to improve

days.title: Warm up the right way
days.goal: Learn a simple warm-up that gets the body ready to move.

video.title: Push-up Exercise Technique

steps: Write a 5-minute warm-up: march in place, arm circles, leg swings.
Do your warm-up and notice how your body feels after.
Add one easy move for the hips and one for the shoulders.
Time your warm-up. It should take about 5 to 10 minutes.
days.task: Do your 5-minute warm-up before any workout this week.
days.challenge: Teach your warm-up to a friend from memory.

quiz.q: Why warm up before exercise?
options: It gets blood moving and lowers injury risk
quiz.explain: A warm-up wakes up the muscles and joints so they move safely.

quiz.q: How long should a warm-up take?
quiz.explain: Five to ten minutes is enough to get the body ready.

quiz.q: What is a good warm-up move?
options: Marching in place with arm circles
quiz.explain: Easy moves that raise the heart rate a little are best.

days.title: Watch how a client moves
days.goal: Learn to spot simple movement problems with your eyes.

video.title: How I Passed The NASM-CPT Certification | NASM Study Guide

steps: Watch a friend squat and note what their knees and back do.
Watch a friend do a push-up and note if their hips sag.
Write down one thing that looked good and one thing to fix.
Practise saying the fix in kind, simple words.
days.task: Watch a friend do 5 squats and write 2 notes: one good, one to fix.
days.challenge: Spot one fix in a video of someone squatting.

quiz.q: What do you watch first in a squat?
quiz.explain: Knees, back and chest tell you if the move is safe.

quiz.q: How should you tell a client about a fix?
options: Kindly, in simple words, one thing at a time
quiz.explain: One kind, simple fix at a time is easy to hear and do.

quiz.q: Why watch before you coach?
options: So your advice matches what you really saw
quiz.explain: Watching first means your advice is true and useful.

days.title: Build a simple full-body workout
days.goal: Learn to build a safe workout with 5 easy moves.

video.title: How to pass NASM Top Vocab Words - Show Up Fitness Study Guide

steps: Pick one move for legs, one for pushing, one for pulling, one for the middle, one for the heart.
Write sets and reps. Sets are groups of reps. Reps are how many times you do a move.
Keep it to 2 sets of 10 reps for a beginner.
Add a warm-up at the start and a cool-down at the end.
days.task: Write a full-body workout on one page.
days.challenge: Build the same workout using only bodyweight moves.

quiz.q: What is a rep?
options: One time you do a move
quiz.explain: A rep is one single time you do the move.

quiz.q: What is a set?
options: A group of reps done together
quiz.explain: A set is a group of reps, like 10 squats in a row.

quiz.q: How many sets suit a beginner?
quiz.explain: Two sets is enough to learn and get stronger without exhaustion.

days.title: Teach a client to breathe well
days.goal: Learn why breathing matters and how to teach it simply.

video.title: ACE-CPT Complete Course | Exercise Science & Personal Training | Full Course on Udemy

steps: Breathe out on the hard part of a move, breathe in on the easy part.
Practise: breathe out as you push up, breathe in as you lower down.
Watch a friend lift and check if they hold their breath.
Write one simple sentence that explains breathing during a lift.
days.task: Teach the breathing rule to a friend in one sentence.
days.challenge: Do 10 squats breathing out on the way up.

quiz.q: When should you breathe out in a lift?
options: On the hard part, when you push or lift
quiz.explain: Breathing out on the hard part keeps you steady and strong.

quiz.q: Why not hold your breath?
options: It can make you dizzy and raise blood pressure
quiz.explain: Holding breath can make you feel dizzy, so keep breathing.

quiz.q: How do you teach breathing simply?
options: One short rule: out on the hard part
quiz.explain: One short rule is easy to remember while moving.

days.title: Rest and recovery are part of training
days.goal: Learn why rest days help clients get stronger.

video.title: What Is The BEST Personal Training Certification? | NASM vs ISSA vs ACE vs ACSM vs NSCA vs NCSF

steps: Write down what happens to muscles after hard work: they repair and grow.
Plan a week with 3 workout days and rest days between them.
List 3 signs a client needs more rest: very sore, tired, weak.
Write one sentence to explain rest to a client.
days.task: Plan a 7-day week with 3 workouts and rest days.
days.challenge: Explain to a friend why muscles grow on rest days.

quiz.q: When do muscles get stronger?
options: During rest, after they repair from training
quiz.explain: Training breaks muscle down a little; rest is when it repairs and grows.

quiz.q: How many rest days should a beginner week have?
quiz.explain: Rest days let the body repair and keep the client fresh.

quiz.q: What is a sign a client needs rest?
options: Feeling very tired, sore or weaker than usual
quiz.explain: Heavy tiredness and soreness are signs to rest more.

days.title: Food basics for a coach
days.goal: Learn the simple food ideas every coach should know.

video.title: ACE Personal Training Certification Review

steps: Learn the 3 main food groups in plain words: protein builds muscle, carbs give energy, fats protect the body.
List 3 protein foods, 3 carb foods and 2 healthy fat foods.
Write a simple plate: half vegetables, a quarter protein, a quarter carbs.
Practise explaining the plate to a friend.
days.task: Draw a simple healthy plate and label the parts.
days.challenge: Name 3 protein foods a client can buy at a local market.

quiz.q: What does protein do?
options: It helps build and repair muscle
quiz.explain: Protein is the building material for muscle.

quiz.q: What do carbs do?
options: They give the body energy to move
quiz.explain: Carbs are the body's main fuel for movement.

quiz.q: What does a healthy plate look like?
options: Half vegetables, a quarter protein, a quarter carbs
quiz.explain: A balanced plate has vegetables, protein and carbs.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 2: Build a 4-week plan
days.goal: Put week 2 together: write a full 4-week beginner plan.

video.title: How To Pass the ACE Personal Trainer Exam | Free ACE CPT Study Guide Included! (2023)

steps: Pick a pretend client: a beginner who wants to get stronger.
Write 3 workouts a week for 4 weeks.
Make each week a little harder: add one rep or one set.
Add rest days and a simple food note to the plan.
days.task: Write the full 4-week plan on two pages.
days.challenge: Explain the plan to a friend in 3 minutes.

quiz.q: How often should a beginner train each week?
quiz.explain: Three times a week gives growth and rest.

quiz.q: How do you make week 2 harder than week 1?
options: Add one rep or one set
quiz.explain: Small adds keep progress safe and steady.

quiz.q: What should a plan include besides moves?
options: Rest days and simple food notes
quiz.explain: Rest and food are part of getting results.

project.title: Build a 4-week beginner plan
project.brief: Write a full 4-week plan for a beginner: 3 workouts a week, rest days, small weekly progress and a food note.
checks: Each week is a little harder
Rest days are in the plan
Food note is simple and clear
Moves are safe for a beginner

days.title: Keep clients coming back
days.goal: Learn simple ways to keep clients motivated and on track.

video.title: How to Build Muscle as a Beginner | Complete Gym Guide

steps: List 3 ways to cheer a client on: praise effort, note progress, set a small win.
Write a short message to a client who missed a week.
Plan a small reward for reaching a goal, like a new workout song.
Write down one question to ask when a client feels stuck.
days.task: Write a kind check-in message to a pretend client.
days.challenge: List 5 small wins you can praise in a session.

quiz.q: What keeps a client motivated?
options: Small wins, praise and clear progress
quiz.explain: Noticing small wins keeps people going.

quiz.q: What should you do when a client misses a week?
options: Check in kindly and help them restart small
quiz.explain: A kind check-in helps them come back without shame.

quiz.q: Why track progress?
options: So the client can see how far they have come
quiz.explain: Seeing progress proves the work is paying off.

days.title: Talk about money and prices simply
days.goal: Learn how to set a fair price and explain it clearly.

video.title: How I'd Start Fitness Coaching From Zero: The First 90 Days

steps: Write what you offer: number of sessions, length, what is included.
Pick a fair price for one session and for a pack of 8 sessions.
Write one clear sentence that explains your price.
Practise saying the price out loud without rushing.
days.task: Write a simple price list for your coaching.
days.challenge: Explain your price to a friend in one calm sentence.

quiz.q: What should a price list show clearly?
options: What is included and how much it costs
quiz.explain: Clear details help clients decide with trust.

quiz.q: Why offer a pack of sessions?
options: It helps clients commit and saves them money
quiz.explain: A pack makes training a habit and rewards commitment.

quiz.q: How should you talk about price?
quiz.explain: Calm and clear talk about money builds trust.

days.title: Stay safe: know your limits
days.goal: Learn when to send a client to a doctor or another expert.

video.title: How To Become A Fitness Coach? Your Ultimate Guide With 10 Essential Steps

steps: List warning signs: chest pain, fainting, sharp joint pain, trouble breathing.
Write a simple rule: if in doubt, stop and get help.
Learn where the nearest first aid kit is in your training space.
Write down the local emergency number.
days.task: Write a one-page safety sheet for your sessions.
days.challenge: Name 3 warning signs that mean stop the workout.

quiz.q: What should you do if a client has chest pain?
options: Stop the workout and get medical help at once
quiz.explain: Chest pain is a warning sign that needs help fast.

quiz.q: What is a red flag during exercise?
options: Sharp pain, dizziness or trouble breathing
quiz.explain: Sharp pain or dizziness means stop and check.

quiz.q: When should a coach send a client to a doctor?
options: When pain or a health problem is beyond coaching
quiz.explain: Coaches handle fitness, not medical problems.

days.title: Grow your coaching business
days.goal: Learn simple steps to find your first paying clients.

video.title: How To Become A Fitness Coach? Your Ultimate Guide: 10 Essential Steps To Becoming A Top Fitness Coach!

steps: Write a short post that says who you help and how.
Ask 3 friends to tell others about your coaching.
Offer one free first session to a new client.
Write down where your clients will find you: gym, park, online.
days.task: Write a short post to find your first client.
days.challenge: Tell 3 people today that you coach beginners.

quiz.q: What is the simplest way to find clients?
options: Tell people you know and help one person well
quiz.explain: Word of mouth from happy clients works best.

quiz.q: Why offer a free first session?
options: So people can try your coaching with no risk
quiz.explain: A free first try builds trust and shows your value.

quiz.q: What should your post say?
options: Who you help and how you help them
quiz.explain: Clear words about who you help bring the right people.

days.title: Teach balance and core simply
days.goal: Learn two easy moves for balance and the middle of the body.

video.title: FREE NASM CPT Study Guide (2026): A 12-Week Plan to Pass

steps: Learn the plank: body straight, hold 10 seconds, breathe.
Practise standing on one leg for 20 seconds each side.
Write 2 cues for the plank and 2 for the one-leg stand.
Add both moves to your full-body workout.
days.task: Add a plank and a one-leg stand to your workout plan.
days.challenge: Hold a plank for 20 seconds with a straight body.

quiz.q: What is the core?
options: The muscles around your belly and lower back
quiz.explain: Core muscles hold your body steady.

quiz.q: What does a plank train?
options: The core and the whole body holding still
quiz.explain: A plank trains the core to hold the body steady.

quiz.q: How can a beginner make a plank easier?
options: Hold for a shorter time or drop to the knees
quiz.explain: Shorter holds or knees down make it doable.

days.title: Cool down and stretch simply
days.goal: Learn a short cool-down that helps the body relax.

video.title: Best Way To Run A First Session With A New Client || Trainer Tips and Solutions

steps: Write a 5-minute cool-down: slow walk, deep breaths, gentle stretches.
Stretch the legs, chest and shoulders for 20 seconds each.
Practise breathing slowly: in for 4 counts, out for 6 counts.
Add the cool-down to the end of your workout plan.
days.task: Do a full cool-down after your next workout.
days.challenge: Teach the cool-down to a friend from memory.

quiz.q: Why cool down after a workout?
options: It helps the heart rate slow down gently
It makes you stronger at once
quiz.explain: A slow cool-down lets the body return to calm safely.

quiz.q: How long should you hold a gentle stretch?
quiz.explain: Twenty seconds is enough to feel the muscle relax.

quiz.q: What is a good cool-down move?
options: A slow walk and deep breaths
quiz.explain: Slow moves and deep breaths calm the body down.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 3: Coach a full session
days.goal: Put week 3 together: coach a full session from warm-up to cool-down.

video.title: Squat Exercise Technique

steps: Write a full session plan: warm-up, 5 moves, cool-down.
Coach a friend through the whole session.
Use your cues and your breathing rule.
Ask your friend what was clear and what was not.
days.task: Coach a full 45-minute session and write what you learned.
days.challenge: Coach the session using only your one-page plan.

quiz.q: What should a full session include?
options: Warm-up, main moves and a cool-down
quiz.explain: A full session warms up, works and cools down.

quiz.q: How do you know the session went well?
options: The client moved safely and understood the cues
quiz.explain: Safe moves and clear cues mean a good session.

quiz.q: What should you do after a session?
options: Write notes on what worked and what to fix
quiz.explain: Notes help you get better each time.

project.title: Coach a full session
project.brief: Coach a full 45-minute session from warm-up to cool-down with a practice client, using your cues and breathing rule.
checks: Session has a warm-up and cool-down
Used clear cues for every move
Asked the client what was clear
Wrote notes on what to fix

days.title: Check progress the simple way
days.goal: Learn easy ways to see if a client is getting better.

video.title: Push-up Exercise Technique

steps: Pick 3 simple tests: how many squats in 1 minute, how long a plank, how far a walk.
Test a friend and write the numbers down.
Repeat the same tests after 2 weeks and compare.
Write one sentence that tells the client what improved.
days.task: Test a friend on 3 simple measures and record the numbers.
days.challenge: Compare two sets of test numbers and find the improvement.

quiz.q: Why test the same way each time?
options: So the numbers can be compared fairly
quiz.explain: Same tests give true comparisons.

quiz.q: What is a good simple test?
options: How many squats in one minute
quiz.explain: A short, simple test is safe and easy to repeat.

quiz.q: How often should you re-test?
quiz.explain: A few weeks apart shows real change without stress.

days.title: Help clients who feel stuck
days.goal: Learn what to do when progress slows down.

video.title: How I Passed The NASM-CPT Certification | NASM Study Guide

steps: List 3 reasons progress slows: too little rest, same routine, eating too little.
Write one small change for each reason.
Practise kind words for a client who feels stuck.
Change one thing in a plan and watch what happens.
days.task: Write 3 fixes for a client who has stopped improving.
days.challenge: Explain a plateau in plain words: progress has paused for now.

quiz.q: What is a plateau?
options: A time when progress pauses even though you train
quiz.explain: A plateau is a flat spot where results pause for a while.

quiz.q: What is a good first fix for a plateau?
options: Change one small thing, like adding a rep
Train twice as hard at once
quiz.explain: One small change shows what works.

quiz.q: What should you say to a stuck client?
options: Kind words and a small next step
quiz.explain: Kind words and a small step keep them going.

days.title: Use simple tools: bands and dumbbells
days.goal: Learn to add bands and dumbbells the safe, simple way.

video.title: How to pass NASM Top Vocab Words - Show Up Fitness Study Guide

steps: Learn what a resistance band is: a stretchy band that adds pull to a move.
Try a band row: hold the band, pull to your belly, squeeze, return slow.
Try a dumbbell press with light weights and a straight back.
Write one safety rule for weights: start light, move slow.
days.task: Try a band row and a light dumbbell press, 2 sets of 10.
days.challenge: Teach a friend the band row in 3 steps.

quiz.q: What is a resistance band?
options: A stretchy band that makes a move harder
quiz.explain: A band adds pull so muscles work harder.

quiz.q: What is the first rule with weights?
options: Move as fast as you can
quiz.explain: Light and slow keeps form safe.

quiz.q: What does a dumbbell press train?
quiz.explain: A press trains the pushing muscles of the upper body.

days.title: Write workout plans that fit real life
days.goal: Learn to fit training into a busy week.

video.title: ACE-CPT Complete Course | Exercise Science & Personal Training | Full Course on Udemy

steps: Ask a pretend client how many days they can train and for how long.
Build a plan for 2 days a week, 30 minutes each.
Build another plan for 4 days a week, 20 minutes each.
Write one tip for training at home with no gym.
days.task: Build a 2-day plan and a 4-day plan for a busy client.
days.challenge: Fit a full workout into 20 minutes on paper.

quiz.q: What matters most in a plan?
options: That it fits the client's real week
quiz.explain: A plan that fits real life is one the client will follow.

quiz.q: How long should a busy client's workout be?
quiz.explain: Short, regular workouts beat long ones that never happen.

quiz.q: What is a good home workout tool?
quiz.explain: Simple tools at home are enough to get stronger.

days.title: Be a coach people trust
days.goal: Learn the habits that make clients trust you for the long run.

video.title: What Is The BEST Personal Training Certification? | NASM vs ISSA vs ACE vs ACSM vs NSCA vs NCSF

steps: List 3 trust habits: show up on time, keep notes, be honest.
Write a short promise you make to every client.
Practise saying I do not know, let me find out.
Write down one thing you will do better next week.
days.task: Write your coach promise in 3 lines.
days.challenge: Be on time for every session this week.

quiz.q: What builds trust fastest?
options: Showing up on time and keeping your word
quiz.explain: Being on time and honest builds trust.

quiz.q: What should you say when you do not know something?
options: I do not know, let me find out
quiz.explain: Honest words keep trust even when you do not know.

quiz.q: Why keep notes on clients?
options: So you remember their goals and progress
quiz.explain: Notes help you coach each person, not just anyone.

days.title: Coach a client with a small injury
days.goal: Learn what to do when a client has a small pain or injury.

video.title: ACE Personal Training Certification Review

steps: Ask the client where it hurts and how bad it is.
Stop the move that hurts.
If the pain is sharp or sudden, stop training and tell them to see a doctor.
Never train through sharp pain.
Write down what happened.
Change the plan to safe moves.
days.task: Write a short plan for a client with a sore knee.
days.challenge: List 3 signs that mean stop training.

quiz.q: What should you do first when a client feels pain?
options: Ask where it hurts and how bad it is
quiz.explain: Asking where it hurts tells you how serious it is.

quiz.q: What kind of pain means stop right away?
quiz.explain: Sharp or sudden pain can mean a real injury.

quiz.q: What should you never do?
quiz.explain: Training through sharp pain can make an injury worse.

days.title: Get ready for your certificate
days.goal: Review the whole course and get your capstone ready.

video.title: How To Pass the ACE Personal Trainer Exam | Free ACE CPT Study Guide Included! (2023)

steps: Read your notes from weeks 1 to 4.
List 5 things you can now do as a coach.
Practise your capstone session once with a friend.
Write down any questions you still have.
days.task: List 5 coaching skills you learned in this course.
days.challenge: Teach one move from memory with no notes.

quiz.q: What is the capstone?
options: A final project that shows what you learned
quiz.explain: The capstone is your final show of skill.

quiz.q: What should you review before the capstone?
options: Your notes from all four weeks
quiz.explain: Reviewing all weeks brings the whole course together.

quiz.q: How do you know you are ready?
options: You can coach a full session safely and clearly
quiz.explain: Coaching a full session well shows you are ready.

days.title: Final practice day
days.goal: Practise your capstone once more, then rest and get ready.

video.title: How to Build Muscle as a Beginner | Complete Gym Guide

steps: Run your capstone session one more time.
Time each part: warm-up, main moves, cool-down.
Fix anything that felt rushed or unclear.
Pack your kit: plan, water, notes, first aid kit.
days.task: Run the capstone session and time each part.
days.challenge: Fix one unclear cue from your practice run.

quiz.q: Why practise the capstone twice?
options: Practice makes the real run calm and smooth
quiz.explain: Practice turns worry into calm confidence.

quiz.q: What should you check the day before?
options: Your plan, your kit and your timing
quiz.explain: Checking your plan and kit avoids last-minute stress.

quiz.q: What is the best way to end a session?
options: A cool-down and a kind word about progress
quiz.explain: A calm end and kind words leave the client happy.

days.title: Capstone day: coach your client
days.goal: Coach a real beginner through a full session and show your skill.

video.title: How I'd Start Fitness Coaching From Zero: The First 90 Days

steps: Welcome your client and talk about their goals.
Run the warm-up, the main workout and the cool-down.
Use clear cues and check how they feel after each move.
Write a short report on how the session went.
days.task: Coach your capstone session and write your report.
days.challenge: Finish your report and hand in your capstone.

quiz.q: What is the first step of the capstone session?
options: Welcome the client and talk about goals
quiz.explain: A warm welcome and a talk set up a safe session.

quiz.q: What should you watch during the session?
options: Form, breathing and how the client feels
quiz.explain: Watching form and feelings keeps the session safe.

quiz.q: What goes in your report?
options: What you did, what worked and what to improve
quiz.explain: A short, honest report shows what you learned.

capstone.title: Coach a real beginner client
capstone.brief: Coach a real beginner through a full session: welcome and goals talk, warm-up, a safe full-body workout, cool-down, and a short written report on how it went.
checks: Welcomed the client and set goals together
Taught each move with clear cues
Listed one thing to improve next time
deliverables: A short video or notes from the session
